summary: Destroy a Writable immediately with Node idempotence, error, and close behavior rather than flushing like end().

target.notes: Mark destroyed immediately, stop normal use, optionally emit error, then close unless emitClose is false; pending writes need not flush. Repeated destroy calls are no-ops apart from internal _destroy behavior.

caveats: destroy(error) is not a graceful end().
Event emission may be deferred by the implementation; preserve Node ordering rather than throwing inline by assumption.

tests.name: destroyed becomes true
tests.input: const {Writable}=require('node:stream'); const w=new Writable({write(c,e,cb){cb()}}); w.destroy(); console.log(w.destroyed);

tests.name: repeated destroy no-op
tests.input: const {Writable}=require('node:stream'); const w=new Writable({write(c,e,cb){cb()}}); w.destroy(); w.destroy(); console.log(w.destroyed);
tests.expected_behavior: prints true without creating a second ordinary destroy transition
